Family Law Practice Guide

Checklist of Essential Documents for Filing Divorce in Nepal Courts

📅 Published: 2025-03-30
🔄 Updated: 2025-10-01
⏱ 6 min read
🔍 Review: Senior Advocate Lead Counsel, Supreme Court Bar Association
Direct Legal Answer & Overview

To initiate divorce proceedings in a Nepal District Court, applicants must assemble: 1) The original or certified Marriage Registration Certificate (or social wedding proof); 2) Nepali Citizenship Certificates of both spouses; 3) Birth Registration Certificates of minor children; 4) Recent passport-sized photographs; 5) A verified property inventory (Lalpurja, bank statements) if partition is claimed; and 6) The formal Plaint (Firdi-patra) or Joint Petition drafted in court format.

Key Practical Takeaways

  • Marriage registration certificate is the foundational document; wedding photos can serve as corroborating proof.
  • NRN citizens require verified passport copies and power of attorney documents.
  • Property ownership documents are required if claiming partition (Ansha) upon divorce.

Preparing accurate, verified documentation is the first practical step toward filing for divorce in Nepal. Missing documents cause procedural rejections at the court registration counter (Darta Phant), delaying court hearings. Below is the comprehensive document checklist mandated by District Courts under the Muluki Civil Procedure Code 2074.

1. Foundational Marital Records

  • Marriage Registration Certificate: Issued by the local municipal ward office. If the marriage was conducted socially without formal registration, provide wedding invitation cards, photographs, and ward relationship verification (Nata Pramanit).
  • Citizenship / Identification: Clear copies of Citizenship Certificates (Nagrikta) of both husband and wife. For non-resident Nepalese (NRNs) or foreign spouses, certified passport copies and marriage registration apostilles are required.

2. Children and Property Records

  • Children Records: Official Birth Registration Certificates for all minor children to establish age for statutory custody parameters.
  • Asset Records: Land Ownership Certificates (Lalpurja), vehicle registrations, bank account summaries, and business shares if seeking matrimonial partition (Ansha) under Section 99.

Statute / Act Section / Rule Legal Significance
Muluki Civil Procedure Code 2074 Chapter 3 Document attachment rules for plaints and petitions filed in District Courts.

Documentary Checklist for this Procedure

  • ✔ Marriage Registration Certificate (Bibaha Darta Pramanpatra)
  • ✔ Citizenship Certificates of applicant(s)
  • ✔ Children birth certificates (if applicable)
  • ✔ Inventory of marital property for partition

Frequently Asked Questions on this Topic

What if the opposing spouse hides or refuses to provide the marriage certificate?

Your advocate can apply to the municipal ward office where the marriage was registered to obtain a certified official duplicate, or submit social wedding evidence with an explanatory affidavit.
